module_title: Modern Physics: Dual Nature and Atomic Models (Detailed Foundational)
introduction: This foundational level bridges the gap between classical physics failures and the birth of Quantum Mechanics. It thoroughly explores the particle nature of light (Photons), the wave nature of matter (De Broglie), and the evolutionary structural models of the atom (Rutherford to Bohr). This is mathematically one of the most high-scoring chapters in NEET and JEE.

core_concepts.title: Photon Theory of Light
core_concepts.description: According to Max Planck and Albert Einstein, light travels in the form of discrete energy packets or bundles called 'Photons'. The energy of each photon is perfectly quantized: $E = h\nu = \frac{hc}{\lambda}$, where $h$ is Planck's constant, $\nu$ is frequency, and $\lambda$ is wavelength. While a photon's rest mass is strictly zero, its kinetic mass is $m = \frac{h}{\lambda c}$ and its momentum is $p = \frac{h}{\lambda}$.

core_concepts.title: The Photoelectric Effect
core_concepts.description: The phenomenon of emission of electrons from a metal surface when light of a suitable frequency (greater than a threshold value) falls on it. The emitted electrons are called 'photoelectrons'. The minimum energy required to just eject an electron from the metal surface is called the Work Function ($W$ or $\Phi$). $W = h\nu_0 = \frac{hc}{\lambda_0}$, where $\nu_0$ is the threshold frequency.

core_concepts.title: De-Broglie Hypothesis (Matter Waves)
core_concepts.description: Louis de Broglie proposed a profound symmetry in nature: if light waves can act as particles (photons), then moving material particles (like electrons, protons) must exhibit wave-like properties. The wavelength of this 'matter wave' is $\lambda = \frac{h}{p} = \frac{h}{mv} = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}}$, where $K$ is the kinetic energy of the particle.

core_concepts.title: Rutherford and Bohr Atomic Models
core_concepts.description: Rutherford discovered the nucleus (where all positive charge and mass are concentrated) via the Alpha-particle scattering experiment. Bohr refined this using quantum theory. Bohr's primary postulate: Electrons can only revolve in specific stable, circular orbits where their Angular Momentum ($L$) is an integral multiple of $\frac{h}{2\pi}$. Mathematically, $L = mvr = \frac{nh}{2\pi}$ (where $n = 1, 2, 3...$ is the principal quantum number).

core_concepts.title: Introduction to Nuclei and Radioactivity
core_concepts.description: The atomic nucleus consists of closely packed protons and neutrons (collectively called nucleons). The radius of a nucleus empirically follows $R = R_0 A^{1/3}$, where $A$ is the Mass Number and $R_0 \approx 1.2 \text{ fm}$ ($1 \text{ fm} = 10^{-15} \text{ m}$). Radioactivity is the spontaneous disintegration of unstable heavy nuclei accompanied by the emission of ionizing radiation ($\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ rays) to achieve stability.

important_entities.name: Planck's Constant ($h$)
important_entities.significance: The fundamental constant of quantum mechanics. For rapid calculations in exams, the product $hc$ is approximated as $1240 \text{ eV nm}$ or $12400 \text{ eV \AA}$. (Example: $E \approx 12400 / \lambda$ yields energy directly in electron-volts if $\lambda$ is in Angstroms).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A pervasive student misconception is that a metal's work function changes if the intensity or frequency of incident light changes. This is absolutely false. The Work Function ($W$) depends EXCLUSIVELY on the nature of the metal (material) and its surface impurities. It is completely independent of the incident light.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Chronological order of spectral series: L (Lyman - drops to n=1), B (Balmer - drops to n=2), P (Paschen - drops to n=3), B (Brackett - drops to n=4), P (Pfund - drops to n=5). Lyman is exclusively in the Ultraviolet (UV) region, Balmer is in the Visible region, and the rest are strictly in the Infrared (IR) region.

exam_strategy_tips: In photoelectric effect problems: Increasing the INTENSITY of light only increases the number of incident photons per second, which proportionally increases the photoelectric current. It has absolutely ZERO effect on the kinetic energy of the emitted electrons or the stopping potential.
